correctness.rationale: The verifier derives an exact forbidden-hypergraph characterization directly from the strong \(\overline{2}\)-separability definition: exactly \(891\) inclusion-minimal obstructions occur and all have size \(4\). A complete normalized include-or-exclude search over all \(27\) ternary words proves maximum size \(10\) and enumerates exactly \(20\) maxima containing \(000\). Coordinatewise symbol permutations expand these to exactly \(54\) labeled maxima, consistent with the independent incidence identity \(20\cdot27=54\cdot10\). Every maximum is then replayed against the original coalition-intersection definition rather than only the forbidden-set test, and the full order-\(1296\) Hamming-isometry action and structural profiles are recomputed.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The later inherited bound for strongly \(\overline{2}\)-separable codes is \(M\le q^{\lceil 2n/3\rceil}+\frac12q^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}(q^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}-1)\); at \((n,q)=(3,3)\) this is \(12\), so it does not determine \(10\). The later paper's sharper length-three equivalence concerns coalition parameter \(3\), not \(2\).

value.rationale: This closes the first ternary length-three instance singled out by the foundational SSC construction: the published construction gives \(9\), the known general upper bound gives \(12\), and the exact value is \(10\). The equality census is structurally informative rather than a routine value lookup: all \(54\) maxima form one Hamming-isometry orbit with stabilizer \(24\) and fixed coordinate and distance profiles. This gives an exact benchmark for a code family introduced specifically to trade weaker combinatorial constraints for more users at linear tracing complexity.
